questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Arrange the coverings of the kidney from within outwards:
questions.explanation: The 4 coverings of the kidney from within outwards are: true or fibrous capsule, formed by collagen-rich connective tissue; perinephric fat or adipose capsule, which occupies the space between the fibrous capsule and renal fascia; renal fascia; and paranephric fat, which occupies the space between the renal fascia and the anterior layer of the thoracolumbar fascia.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following fascia attaches the perirenal fascia to the peritoneum?
questions.explanation:
The lateroconal fascia attaches the perirenal fascia to the peritoneum. It extends from the lateral margin of perirenal fascia and attaches to the parietal peritoneum. Option A: Gerota's fascia is the perirenal fascia. The kidney and the suprarenal gland are enclosed within anterior and posterior lamina of the perirenal fascia. The anterior lamina of the perirenal fascia blends with the connective tissue surrounding the great vessels behind the duodenum and pancreas. The posterior lamina continues as the lateroconal fascia. Option C: Thoracolumbar fascia is a complex arrangement of multiple fascial layers in the thoracolumbar region. This fascia encloses the paraspinal muscles, quadratus lumborum muscle and the latissimus dorsi muscle. Option D: Treitz's fascia has been used to refer to the fusion fascia behind the head of pancreas.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the structure into which the renal papillae open?
questions.explanation: The renal papillae open into the minor calyces. The papilla is the conical apex of a renal pyramid, where the urine from the collecting ducts enters into the minor calyces. The minor calyces unite to form the major calyces, which further unite to form the renal pelvis. The kidney is divided into an outer cortex and an inner medulla. The renal medulla contains many striated and conical pyramids. The base of the pyramid is peripherally located, whereas the apex is directed towards the renal sinus (hilum). The renal cortex is subcapsular and arches over the bases of the pyramids. It extends between the pyramids towards the renal sinus as renal columns. questions.question: A 56-year-old male was brought to the emergency department with severe pain in the left flank region. CT examination revealed occlusion of the left renal vein. The condition would impede the blood flow through all of the following veins except:

questions.question: A 42-year-old man presented with severe pain in the lower back radiating to the pubic symphysis. Ultrasonography revealed a stone in the left ureter, measuring 3 mm in size. The stone is most likely to be lodged in which of the following sites?
questions.explanation:
Vesicoureteric junction is the narrowest part of the ureter. This is the reason why stones as small as 2 to 3 mm get arrested in the vesicoureteric junction. The ureter is constricted at 5 places: + Pelvi-ureteric junction + Brim of the lesser pelvis (as it crosses the common iliac artery) + Point of crossing of the ureter by ductus deferens or broad ligament of the uterus. + Vesico-ureteric junction

+ Opening in the lateral angle of the trigone These are regarded as surgical constrictions of the ureter. However, only 1, 2, and 4 are the anatomical constrictions of the ureter. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following lobes of the prostate forms the uvula vesicae?
questions.explanation:
The median lobe of the prostate forms the uvula vesicae.

Uvula vesicae is an elevation in the mucous membrane of the urinary bladder, behind the internal

urethral orifice. It is often enlarged in benign prostatic hypertrophy.

questions.question: Where does the internal urethral orifice lie at birth?

options.text: At the level of the umbilicus
At the level of the lower border of symphysis pubis
At the level of the perineal body
At the level of the upper border of symphysis pubis

questions.correctAnswerText: At the level of the upper border of symphysis pubis
questions.explanation:
The interna] urethral orifigesie’ at the level of the upper border of the pubic symphysis at birth.

At birth, he bladder is aitabdominal organ. But as the child grows, the blader descends, and near

puberty, it becomes a pelvic organ.

In an adult, the internal urethral orifice lies 3-4 cm behind the lower part of the pubic symphysis.

It corresponds to the bladder neck.

Clinical note: As the bladder lies above the symphysis pubis, we can safely perform suprapubic

needle punctures to obtain urine samples in children. But in adults, this can only be done if the

bladder is fully distended.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures is innervated by the neurons present in Onuf's nucleus?
questions.explanation: The external urethral sphincter is innervated by neurons present in Onuf's nucleus. The neurons present in lamina IX of the grey matter in spinal segments S2, S3, and S4 constitute Onuf's nucleus and contract the external urethral sphincter. The external urethral sphincter is skeletal muscle; contraction maintains urinary continence. Just before voiding, it relaxes because neurons in Onuf's nucleus are centrally inhibited by the brain. The source also provides a diagram locating Onuf's nucleus and a comparison table of parasympathetic and sympathetic nerve supply to the bladder.
